transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Well, what brings me in... I guess it's because I feel like I'm always moving from one thing to the next, you know? Like I can't just idle. It's funny, my old car was like that, an '86 Chevy Nova, couldn't idle for a minute without stalling out at a red light. I had to keep my foot on the gas and the brake at the same time just to keep it running. Anyway, the new work setup has made it a lot harder to hide that I can't sit still. I've been doing customer service for years, but they changed our phone system and the desks, and now... well, it's just different. I used to be able to pace more when I was on hold with a customer. Do you ever get put on hold and just have to walk around the room?
Can you tell me if you've felt this restless, always-needing-to-move feeling since you were a kid, or is this something that's only started more recently, say in the last several months?

Oh, no, it's definitely not a new thing. I mean, looking back, this has been around long before the job change. Even when I was just a kid, way back in grade school... I remember my teachers always writing on my report cards that I was, you know, bright but careless. They said I talked out of turn a lot and always had to be reminded to stay with my work. Actually, speaking of report cards, my mother kept all of them in this old shoebox. It was one of those sturdy Buster Brown boxes, you remember those? She had this whole system in the attic where she kept everything—report cards, my little league trophies, even some old baseball cards. I think I had a Mickey Mantle rookie card in there somewhere, but my brother probably swiped it when we were teenagers. He was always doing stuff like that, taking my things without asking. We used to get into these huge arguments over it, especially about my records. I had this great collection of classic rock vinyl, and he'd just leave them out of the sleeves... but yeah, anyway, the teachers always said I had trouble just sitting there and focusing.
Aside from being restless, do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks, follow through on details, or keep things organized, even in situations where you're not moving around?

Yeah, definitely. It's like... well, with work, I'll think I've completely finished a customer ticket, right? I'll hit submit, feel good about it, and then later I realize I typed the wrong account number, or I just completely skipped one of those required little boxes. Or I miss one tiny instruction and the whole thing gets bounced back to me. It's so frustrating. It actually reminds me of this time I was trying to put together a gas grill I bought at Home Depot. I thought I had all the parts laid out perfectly on the patio. It was a nice day, too, I think it was right around Memorial Day, maybe a few years ago. My neighbor, Dave, was outside mowing his lawn. He has one of those riding mowers, a John Deere, really nice machine. I always wanted one, but my yard isn't quite big enough to justify it, you know? Anyway, Dave waves over, and I'm putting this grill together, and I get to the very end, and there's this one little washer left over. Just one piece. And I realize I missed a step way back on page two, and I had to take half the thing apart just to put it in. But yeah, the tickets at work... I make those kinds of little mistakes all the time.
Do these struggles with restlessness and staying organized cause noticeable problems for you not just at work, but also at home or in your personal relationships?

Well, at home, I guess my wife gets on my case sometimes about half-finished projects, like that grill I was talking about. But it's really at work where it's becoming a big headache. It's actually started showing up in my performance reviews lately. My supervisors keep pointing out all these unfinished tickets and the little mistakes I make. They say it slows the whole team down. And I'm really trying hard, you know? I generally get along great with the customers. In fact, just last week I had this lovely older lady on the phone, Mrs. Higgins. She was having trouble with her billing, and we ended up talking for twenty minutes about her grandson who plays the cello. My nephew used to play the cello, actually. He was quite good, went to state competitions and everything. My sister always had to lug that huge case around in her minivan. She had one of those early 2000s Dodge Caravans, the ones with the sliding doors that always got stuck in the winter... but yeah, my boss says the mistakes are a problem, even if the customers like me.
